$comment: LIVE-1 / ADR-0165 — the CubeSandbox template contract for the live display.
specVersion 4 (2026-08-18, LIVE-5c). specVersion 2 was a DECLARED contract;
specVersion 3 (#1438) recorded the MEDIA half as measured end to end on
momo-cube-host (101.79.18.230) + momo-turn (223.130.142.109) — a real microVM
producer whose H264 screen reached an external browser over a TURN-relayed
WebRTC stream. specVersion 4 records the INPUT half: a work-host-signed
validate, a datachannel the producer opens only while the server grants it,
declared frames parsed and injected with XTEST, and the channel closing when
the window closes while the stream stays up.
What is still unverified is ONE thing, and it is named rather than implied:
the input round trip INSIDE a CubeSandbox microVM, over a relay candidate
(`unverified.inputDeliveryInMicroVM`). The media half already ran there; the
input half so far has run against the same producer image elsewhere.
verify with scripts/verify_display_attach.sh (cross-reads server constants)
and scripts/display_input_e2e.py (the input half, inside the template image).

runtimeVerified.$comment: #1438 measured 2026-08-16 (media). LIVE-5c measured 2026-08-18 (input). #1438 evidence: external Chromium rendered display-e2e-1438 at 1280x720, 56 frames decoded, media candidate pair relay<->relay; coturn logged ALLOCATE+CHANNEL_BIND success from BOTH the producer (101.79.18.230) and the browser (39.115.69.188), over TURN transport=udp AND transport=tcp. LIVE-5c evidence, all from scripts/display_input_e2e.py against THIS producer image: (a) a work-host-SIGNED validate answered input_enabled=true and the offer carried m=application; (b) key frames encoded to signalling.inputChannel were parsed and injected with XTEST, and the typed command RAN in a real terminal on the captured X display — the proof is the file it wrote, not the frames sent; (c) the same harness with an OBSERVER capability got input_enabled=false and an offer with NO m=application; (d) when the control window was closed server-side, the channel closed, the peer connection and signalling socket STAYED UP, and a command typed afterwards did not run — measured while the signalling socket was being flooded with frames the message loop discards, because that is the case where a re-validation in the wrong place starves. Measured on the template image, NOT inside a CubeSandbox microVM — see unverified.inputDeliveryInMicroVM.

$comment: The template is built by `cubemastercli tpl create-from-image` from an OCI
image, NOT by systemd. PID 1 is the #1437 bootstrap receiver, which lands
the create-time envVars delivery and then execs the entrypoint.
MUST be built WITHOUT `--probe`: the producer legitimately does not listen
on :8452 until after the create-time delivery arrives, and no delivery
happens during a template build. A display template built with --probe or
without the receiver fails EVERY envVars create with 500 (130497), which is
the exact state the real T3 adapter provisions in (#1437/#1434).
template.ordering: entrypoint.sh, not a systemd unit — adds the ICE base (see network.iceBase), starts Xvfb, waits on the X socket, then execs the producer
template.$requiresIproute2Comment: iproute2 must be in the rootfs so entrypoint can add the routable ICE base; without it, relay gathering fails (see network.iceBase).

$comment: ADR-0165 D1 named Selkies-GStreamer first with `webrtcbin` as the
alternative; this template declares the alternative on the D4 structural
argument (view-only = ABSENCE of an input datachannel). #1438 RESOLVED the
producerSelection unknown: webrtcbin encodes H264 acceptably inside a
GPU-less microVM and an external browser decoded 56 frames at 1280x720.
Swapping the producer is still a one-field change here plus the unit file;
nothing in server-rust names a producer.
producer.$inputComment: ADR-0165 D4, as amended by inputDatachannelOnDemand. RUNTIME-VERIFIED twice: #1438 measured that the OBSERVER offer carries m=video a=sendonly and NO m=application against a real producer through the host proxy; LIVE-5c measured that the same producer, handed a CONTROLLER grant the server vouched for, offers m=application and delivers keystrokes — and that revoking the grant closes the channel while the stream keeps running. `inputDatachannel: false` below stays the DEFAULT and the observer's guarantee; it is not a global switch (there is no MOMO_DISPLAY_INPUT=1).

inputDatachannelOnDemand.$comment: LIVE-3 / ADR-0004 증보 3. RUNTIME-VERIFIED (LIVE-5c): the producer reads input_enabled off its OWN validate answer, opens the channel between READY and PLAYING so it lands in the first offer, and closes it at the re-validation that first answers false — measured by closing the window server-side and watching the channel close while the stream stayed up. A viewer's `open_input` is still refused by name: asking is not authorisation. The re-validation runs at the TOP of the producer's message loop, where no discarded frame can skip it; a viewer that could starve it would keep a keyboard the server had already taken away.
inputDatachannelOnDemand.closedOn: the first re-validation answering input_enabled == false

producer.$bundlePolicyComment: MEASURED (LIVE-5c), not a preference. webrtcbin defaults to bundle-policy `none`, which gives each m-line its own ICE component and DTLS transport. That was invisible while the offer had one m-line (#1438 measured video only); the moment the input channel adds m=application, `none` produced ICE reaching `completed` and the connection then going `failed` in DTLS — a screen that connects and a keyboard that never arrives, with nothing naming the cause. Browsers negotiate max-bundle, so this is also the only policy the real web viewer was ever going to answer with.

hostProxy.$comment: ADR-0165 증보 1 D2-1. RUNTIME-VERIFIED (#1438): external browser -> wss://<host-public>:8443/display/signal/<displayId> -> nginx (형상 A, client-IP preserving) -> microVM :8452. TLS is self-signed in the E2E; a real cert is a follow-up (runbook §9 item 2).

$comment: LIVE-5b declared this block; LIVE-5c implemented the producer half against
it and MEASURED it (scripts/display_input_e2e.py). It is written here rather
than in one client because this is the one file both halves read: the web
client (clients/web/src/features/work/controlStream.ts) cross-reads it in
controlStream.test.ts, and the producer parses exactly these shapes.
OPENED BY THE PRODUCER, NEVER BY THE VIEWER. The trigger is the
producer's own validate answer (producer.inputDatachannelOnDemand), so a
viewer that opened its own channel would be routing around the server's
grant. The web client therefore has no createDataChannel and does not
encode open_input; it listens on ondatachannel, and the producer still
refuses `open_input` by name.
The key frame carries `code` (the PHYSICAL key) and modifiers, never the
character the browser produced from them. A remote keyboard is physical
keys plus the far side's layout, and it means the character of a
password never forms as a value this browser client owns (ADR-0004 증보 3
D2). The producer ENFORCES that rather than assuming it: a frame carrying
`key`, `char` or `text` is refused.
The field names survived first contact unchanged — LIVE-5c corrected no
part of this block, which is the outcome the split-by-action pointerFrame
shape below was written to produce.
inputChannel.label: momo.input.v1

$comment: DECLARED PER ACTION, not as one flat field list. A flat list reads as
'these fields are always present', and a producer built from that
reading requires `button` on every pointer frame — so a MOVE, which
carries none, is dropped, clicks keep working and the cursor never
travels. That failure is invisible in a paper contract and obvious on
a screen, so the shape is split here where both halves read it.
`button` is ABSENT on a move rather than sent as 0: a move with button
0 and a left-button drag are different events, and a sentinel makes
them the same one.

inputChannel.pointerCoordinates: normalised 0..1 over the video box, so the VM's resolution stays the VM's
inputChannel.$refusalComment: A frame the producer will not inject is counted and logged BY REASON, never echoed and never logged as a frame: a log holding a sequence of key frames is a keylogger written by accident.
$keyFrameComment: The producer injects the PHYSICAL KEY EVENT and nothing else: `code` becomes
one XTEST key press or release, and `ctrl`/`shift`/`alt`/`meta`/`repeat` are
read by NO ONE on the producer side.
That is deliberate, and it is why the modifiers stay declared. The web client
forwards a modifier press as its OWN key frame (`ShiftLeft` down arrives
before the character it shifts, and its up arrives after), so the far side
holds real modifier state from real key events. Synthesising modifiers from
these booleans AS WELL would apply them twice — a shifted character typed
with the shift already physically down.
So they are carried as CONTEXT, for a viewer or a log to reason about intent,
never as an instruction. A producer that started honouring them would need
the client to stop sending modifier keys in the same change.

$policyComment: (D3-1) established relay is the only viable path (symmetric NAT). #1438
measured a DEEPER reason the producer must force relay AND the template
must supply a routable ICE base: see network.iceBase.

turn.credentialDelivery: per-session ephemeral (LIVE-5a): the producer reads `ice_servers` off its own display-attach/validate answer and renders it into webrtcbin's `turn://` spelling at pipeline construction. The pre-LIVE-5a static long-term cred delivered via envVars (#1437 receiver) as MOMO_DISPLAY_TURN_URI is now the FALLBACK: an instance whose momo-server was given no MOMO_TURN_STATIC_AUTH_SECRET answers `ice_servers: []` and the static path carries it unchanged.
turn.credentialPreference: server-minted wins over the envVars static whenever `ice_servers` is non-empty
$credentialRefreshComment: MEASURED (LIVE-5c, coturn 4.6 with use-auth-secret, TTL forced to 60s).
The reasoning this replaces was: the server re-mints on every validate,
the producer installs one credential at pipeline construction and throws
the later mints away (GStreamer cannot swap a TURN server on a running
ICE agent, and reading `webrtcbin.ice-agent` DESTROYS the agent), so the
TTL must be a ceiling on the peer connection and the screen must go black
It does not. A stream held for 200s on a 60s credential lost NOTHING: 10
of 10 typed beats were delivered, the last at t+180s, over a relay-only
producer. coturn re-validates the REST username's expiry when an
ALLOCATE creates an allocation; it does not re-check it to REFRESH an
allocation that already exists, and the refreshes kept succeeding under
So the TTL bounds when a NEW allocation can be created, not how long a
running one lives. The re-mint the producer discards is genuinely
surplus for an established connection. The narrow case that remains is a
connection that has to allocate AGAIN mid-session (an ICE restart), which
wants a fresh credential at THAT moment rather than a periodic swap.
$credentialComment: The server mint is coturn's `use-auth-secret` derivation:
SHA-1 is fixed by WebRTC's STUN MESSAGE-INTEGRITY rather than chosen —
MEASURED 2026-08-18 against the LIVE momo-turn (223.130.142.109) from an
external Mac, RFC 5766 ALLOCATE: the STATIC credential still allocates over
udp AND tcp (relayed 223.130.142.109:*, lifetime 600s, realm oort.turn), and
an EPHEMERAL credential is refused 401 — `use-auth-secret` is NOT yet enabled
on the relay. So the server half of this contract is landed and proved in
conformance while the relay half is an operator step, in that order and never
the reverse: momo-turn carries production traffic, and the static credential
is not removed until the ephemeral one is measured working beside it
turn.$comment: CHANGED from null. #1438 RESOLVED iceReachability: the producer allocates a relay on momo-turn and the browser connects relay<->relay. coturn logged ALLOCATE success from the microVM (via host egress 101.79.18.230) over both udp and tcp.

ice.requiresAdrAmendment: ADR-0165 증보 2 — turn is now REQUIRED (was 'introduce only if measured necessary'). #1438 is that measurement. The producer forces iceTransportPolicy=relay and the template supplies a routable ICE base.

$comment: CHANGED to enforced:false. GStreamer 1.22 webrtcbin has NO port-range
property, and reading `ice-agent` to reach the underlying ICE object
DESTROYS it (over-unref → later negotiation dies on GST_IS_WEBRTC_ICE
assertion) — do not read it. The microVM media ports are therefore not
constrained here. In the relay topology it does not matter: media does
not ingress to the microVM on these ports — it egresses to the TURN and
is relayed, so the ports that face the internet are momo-turn's
49152-65535 range, not these.
NEW in specVersion 3 — the #1438 root-cause finding. A CubeSandbox
microVM's guest eth0 carries ONLY link-local addresses (IPv4
169.254.68.6/30, IPv6 fe80::). libnice (webrtcbin's ICE stack) REGISTERS
the TURN but schedules NO STUN/TURN candidate discovery from a link-local
base — measured 'Candidate gathering FINISHED, no scheduled items' — so
the producer emits ZERO candidates and cannot allocate a relay, even
though the TURN works and the microVM can reach it (raw-socket STUN got a
reply). The fix, measured to work: entrypoint adds a routable RFC1918
address to eth0 (default 10.99.0.2/24) BEFORE the producer starts. libnice
then uses it as a base, allocates the relay, and the CubeNet gateway
MASQUERADEs the flow out the host's public IP and returns the reply.
The identical producer needed no such fix in a container (it already had
an RFC1918 172.17.x address) — this is specific to the microVM's
link-local-only posture.
iceBase.addedBy: entrypoint (needs iproute2 + CAP_NET_ADMIN, which PID1 in a microVM has)

unverified.$comment: specVersion 2's producerSelection / iceReachability / templateBuild are RESOLVED (see runtimeVerified). LIVE-5c resolved inputChannelProtocol, inputDelivery and serverValidateWiring on the template image, and MEASURED credentialCeiling. What remains is the CubeSandbox/TURN leg of the input path and the two items that wait on a human.
unverified.inputDeliveryInMicroVM: THE REMAINING HALF OF LIVE-5c. Input delivery is measured against this producer image (runtimeVerified.keystrokeReachesAnApplication) but NOT yet inside a CubeSandbox microVM on momo-cube-host, and therefore not yet over a `typ relay` candidate end to end. The template that carries the input half IS built and READY on the host (momo-display4, 2026-08-18); what stopped the host run is that the producer's validate needs a momo-server the microVM can reach, and standing one up on momo-cube-host was outside this goal's permissions. #1438 already measured the media leg over relay, and LIVE-5c measured the input leg over a real ICE/DTLS/SCTP datachannel, so what is unmeasured is specifically the two together on the host.
unverified.realTlsCert: The host proxy used a self-signed cert in the E2E (browser launched with ignore-cert-errors). A real cert/domain is a follow-up (runbook §9 item 2). The producer now VERIFIES against a named certificate rather than skipping verification: MOMO_DISPLAY_SERVER_CA_PEM_B64 lands a bundle and MOMO_DISPLAY_SERVER_CA_BUNDLE points at it; with neither, https validate verifies against the system store and a self-signed proxy fails closed.
unverified.relayCredentialRetirement: The ephemeral credential path is landed on BOTH sides (server mints, producer prefers) and proved in conformance, but momo-turn itself still runs `lt-cred-mech` + a static `user=` line — measured 2026-08-18: static ALLOCATE succeeds, ephemeral ALLOCATE is 401. Enabling `use-auth-secret` on the relay, measuring both credentials side by side, and only then deleting the `user=` line is docs/runbooks/turn-host-install.md §6 and has NOT been performed (#1545, a 성재-hand step). LIVE-5c measured the ephemeral path against a LOCAL coturn 4.6 with use-auth-secret instead.
